Thanks for the summary — that matches our internal notes. A few clarifications and a quick data point attached.

Traffic details (confirmed):
- Steady-state: 18–22 QPS sustained for recommendation endpoint (weekday baseline).
- Promo spikes: we see up to 120–140 QPS for ~10–20 minutes during campaign bursts, roughly 2–3 times per week.
- Typical request: ~3–8 input tokens, ~6–12 output tokens on average.
- We need p95 < 200ms for the request/response (hard SLA for our frontend). p50 can be much lower.

Constraints:
- SOC 2 compliance is a must (we can share our questionnaire).
- Data residency: most traffic is US-based but we have EU customers; if there’s a simple region-routing option that’s great but not blocker for the pilot.

Ask from our side:
- Please include a Dedicated sizing + cost as a comparison. If Dedicated can reliably meet p95 <200ms during peak without complex client-side sharding, that’s preferred.
- If you can show a Hosted + Dedicated fallback path (i.e., Hosted for baseline with Dedicated reserved capacity during promos), we’d like an operational sketch of how failover and routing would work.

Attached: quickhaul_prod_traffic.csv (sample), I can also export a 7-day window if helpful.

Thanks — will wait on the two-option plan and cost comparison.

Elena / Samir —

Appreciate the quick detail and the traffic CSV — super helpful. Based on the numbers you sent, here are two concrete pilot options we recommend for evaluation, with the metrics we would instrument during the pilot.

Option A — Hosted-first, Dedicated fallback:
- Hosted API serves steady-state (18–22 QPS).
- Automatic routing to Dedicated pool when internal queue depth or latency exceeds threshold (spike window routing).
- Pros: fastest time-to-live, no infra commitments; cons: potential cold-start / tail-latency risk on extreme peaks.
- Expected p95 (estimate): Hosted with optimized batching ~ 160–240ms depending on model choice and burst; Dedicated fallback should keep p95 < 200ms for most peaks.

Option B — Dedicated reserved pilot:
- Dedicated pool sized for sustained baseline (approx 1x capacity to handle 22 QPS with headroom and 2–3 replica autoscale for short bursts).
- Pros: predictable latency and throughput, simpler SLO guarantees; cons: reservation cost.
- Expected p95 (estimate): Dedicated with continuous batching & KV-cache likely hitting p95 < 150–180ms at steady and under short spikes (subject to model selection).

Pilot scope / instrumentation (both options):
- Metric set: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail latency percentiles during promos, error rate, tokens/sec, average batch size, queue depth.
- Duration: 2–4 week pilot recommended (1 week smoke + 1–3 weeks with promo event sample).
- Success criteria: p95 < 200ms for 95% of non-error requests and no more than 2 SLO breaches during promo windows.

Ben — can you run a rough cost delta for Option A (hosted baseline + scaling) vs Option B (1–2 month reserved pilot for Dedicated). I’ll assemble a short pilot doc and timeline and circulate.

Attachments: redwood_pilot_options_v1.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

Next steps summary:
1) Ben provides cost delta (EOD 10/08).
2) We (Avery) produce a 1-page pilot doc with routing sketch and rollback plan.
3) QuickHaul confirms pilot dates and provides SOC 2 questionnaire.
